findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a CI-mode builder fixes a failing test after another repair test passed.
The new CI sentence leaves the unconditional instruction at src/forge/templates/brief.md:231 to “Rerun only what failed”, so the builder cannot choose to rerun the passing repair test after changing the code. Also, src/forge/worker.py:626 and :739-740 insert the test-audit authoring gate into initial and resumed briefs; .codex/skills/test-audit/SKILL.md:43-45 still requires a regression test to demonstrably fail before the fix and pass afterwards. The brief therefore still dictates repair testing and its red-then-green order.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a nightly or manually requested full test run.
The edited skill no longer matches the SHA-256 pinned in tests/test_trim_skills.py:31-33. Its test compares the current bytes with that pin at lines 59-60 and fails before checking wheel, source-distribution and editable-install sync. The nightly workflow runs the full suite, so its result will be red until the obsolete pin is updated for this deliberate change.
findings.title: Functional: Keep the full-suite skill packaging test passing

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a new or earlier-adopted client syncs its worker guidance.
This test checks that the skill's validation section contains the CI boundary sentence, but that sentence was also present alongside the old mandatory repair-test instructions. tests/test_builders_check_exact_repair_tests.py:50-53 makes the same positive-only check. Restoring the old skill validation text would leave these assertions passing; the brief's negative assertion does not cover it because src/forge/worker.py:739-740 embeds only the skill's authoring section. The named proof therefore cannot detect the old instructions reaching either host after sync.
findings.title: Gate: Check the removed instructions in synced test-audit skills

stop.reason: Harm 3 findings: one more round by the standing rule

why: The worker brief spells out red-then-green steps for CI-mode builders, which agents do anyway; the only rule needed is that wider related tests, lint and type checks stay in pull request CI
